definitions.gloss: everything; anything and everything; all things without exception
definitions.explanation: Emphasizes totality — that absolutely nothing is left out. Often carries an emotional nuance of being overwhelmed or resigned.

examples.japanese: {何|なに}もかも{嫌|いや}になった。
{彼|かれ}は{何|なに}もかも{知|し}っているようだ。
{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}しで{何|なに}もかも{新|あたら}しい{生活|せいかつ}が{始|はじ}まった。
examples.english: With the move, a completely new life began with everything fresh.

notes:
An emphatic way to say "everything" that stresses completeness — nothing at all is excluded. Often appears in emotional contexts expressing frustration, resignation, or awe.

USAGE:
Typically used as the subject or object of a sentence. The particle を or が often follows, though it can also function adverbially.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {何|なに}もかも{捨|す}てる: to throw away everything
- {何|なに}もかも{忘|わす}れる: to forget everything
- {何|なに}もかもうまくいく: everything goes well
- {何|なに}もかも{嫌|いや}になる: to get sick of everything

SIMILAR WORDS:
- すべて: everything — neutral and formal; lacks the emotional emphasis
- {全部|ぜんぶ}: all; the whole lot — conversational but matter-of-fact
- {何|なに}もかにも: everything — variant form with similar meaning but less common
